segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: Allow me to say my opening remarks.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: To our distinguished chairperson, Kong Mika Swansing,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: my fellow vice chairperson and colleagues in the House of Representatives,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: to our tourism secretary, Dita Angara Mathay,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: and the hardworking team of the Department of Tourism,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: good evening and welcome to the Department's budget briefing.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: It is a privilege to preside over our deliberations on a sector that continues to generate jobs,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: and showcase to the world why they should love the Philippines,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: while encouraging Filipinos and visitors alike to discover more to love across our country.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: This evening, we have the opportunity to hear from the Department of Tourism,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: and to hear from our newly appointed Tourism Secretary, Sec. Dita Angara Mathay,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: who has taken on the important responsibility of leading this vital sector.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: At the same time, it is our duty in Congress to constructively examine

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: whether the Department's proposed budget responds to the needs of Philippine tourism,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: and whether every peso we invest translates into more visitors,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: and more opportunities for our people.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: and the importance of this sector is clear from the numbers.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: In 2025, tourism generated 2.27 trillion in tourism direct gross value added,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: equivalent to 8.1% of our GDP, while supporting millions of Filipino jobs.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: Tourism, therefore, is not merely about destinations and visitor arrivals.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: It is a major contributor to our economy, and more importantly, to the livelihood of our people.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: These figures remind us why today's economy is so important,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: and why this budget deliberation matters.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: We must ensure that the resources we provide to the Department

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: are commensurate with both the opportunities and the challenges facing Philippine tourism.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: As a tourism advocate, this is a sector I've always felt deeply connected.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: Coming from Sorsogon, I have seen firsthand how tourism can transform communities

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: and create opportunities for our people.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: Kasama po ako sa mga naniniwala that we should invest more in Philippine tourism.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: And so I look forward to a productive and constructive deliberation,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: one where we recognize our gains, identify where we can do better,

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: and determine how Congress and the DOT can work together to make tourism

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: an even stronger driver of inclusive and sustainable growth.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: With that, may I now invite Sec. Dita Angara-Mathai

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: to present the Department's proposed budget and priorities.

segments.speaker: Rep. Marie Bernadette G. Escudero
segments.text: Madam Secretary, you may now proceed.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Tourism has been creating value for our economy and our people.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: we intend to turn this momentum into greater economic value

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: May I now present the Department of Tourism's performance and direction for Fiscal Year

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: First, our performance and accomplishments for 2025, second, the DOT's proposed budget

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: under the Fiscal Year 2027 National Expenditure Program, and third, the additional funding

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: requirements needed to sustain our momentum and drive the next phase of tourism growth.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Our mandate is to lead the planning, development, promotion and coordination of Philippine tourism.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: We deliver this as one department.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The Central Office sets policy and strategic direction.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Our regional offices develop destinations and tourism products, while our foreign offices

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: build markets and generate international demand.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Our agencies and corporations extend the Department's work across the tourism ecosystem, providing

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: specialized support in infrastructure, heritage and destination development, dive tourism,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: retirement, visitor services and tourism promotion.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: In terms of funding, our NGAs are directly funded through appropriations in the GAA,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: while our GOCCs generally operate under their corporate operating budgets.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: For Fiscal Year 2027, both Duty Free Philippines and the Tourism Promotion Board have proposed

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Our work is delivered through four core programs, with branding as a dedicated sub-program under

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Tourism Policy and Planning sets the direction for the development of tourism in Philippine

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Tourism Industry Training develops our people.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Standards Development and Enforcement ensures quality.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Market and Product Development turns our tourism assets into experiences that people

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: can visit, enjoy and spend on.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Branding Campaign brings these experiences to the market, strengthening the Philippine

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: tourism brand and converting interest into actual travel.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: These programs connect strategy, people, quality, products and markets into one tourism development

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The programs must translate into measurable outcomes.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Tourism Direct Gross Value Added measures tourism's contribution to the economy.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Tourism expenditures show how visitor activity translates into spending.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Tourism Employment tells us how that activity creates jobs.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: jobs. Tourism arrivals measure our ability to attract visitors to the Philippines. Together,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: these indicators tell us not only how tourism is performing, but how much value it has created

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: for the country and for Filipinos. And the numbers show the scale of tourism's contribution to the

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: economy. In 2025, tourism directly generated 2.27 trillion in economic value, equivalent to 8.1%

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: of our GDP. Tourism spending was also substantial, with 3.26 trillion pesos generated by domestic

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: tourism and 698 billion pesos from international visitors. This shows that tourism is a major

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Tourism spending generates jobs and supports businesses and livelihoods across the country.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Let's look closely into the economic value of tourism, particularly to the creation of job

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: opportunities and livelihoods for millions of Filipinos. In 2025, tourism supported 7.7 million

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: jobs, representing 15.7% of total employment in the country. That is nearly

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: One in every six working Filipinos with tourism employment continuing to grow from 5.4 million in

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: 2021. That economic activity is supported by continued tourism demand. From January to July

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: 2026, international visitor arrivals reached 3.93 million, up by 1.5% from 3.87 million

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: during the same period last year. The United States,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: of course, remains our largest source market, followed by South Korea and Japan, while China

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: has returned to make top-five markets. The challenge now is to build on these key markets

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: and accelerate international tourist arrivals through the rest of the year.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The current performance builds on the recovery achieved over the past three years. Visitor

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Sustaining that upward trajectory now requires us to compete more effectively for a larger

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: share of the regional tourism market.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: But our performance must also be viewed with an increasingly competitive ASEAN tourism

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: In 2025, the Philippines ranked 6th in ASEAN, improving from 7th place in 2024.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Yet, with 6.48 million arrivals, we captured only 5 percent of the regional market shown

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Our improved ranking is encouraging, but the opportunity is much larger.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Our task ahead is to compete for a greater share of ASEAN tourist arrivals.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Beyond tourist volume, our objective is to increase the economic value generated by every

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The Philippines remained 5th in ASEAN in tourism receipts in 2025, generating about 12.15

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: While receipts declined slightly from 2024, our regional position was maintained despite

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The opportunity now is to attract more visitors and generate greater value from every visit.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Our regional position must also be viewed in the context of the resources behind tourism

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: In 2025, the Philippines operated with about 49.7 million dollars, significantly below

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: the tourism budget of the major ASEAN destinations shown here.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Yet, tourism already contributes 2.27 trillion to our economy and supports 7.7 million Philippine

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: We are emphasizing that greater strategic investment in tourism can unlock a much larger

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: opportunity as it can bring more tourists, generate more spending, create more jobs,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: and spread socio-economic growth across our regions.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The investment opportunity becomes even more important.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The opportunity becomes even clearer when we look at tourism marketing budgets of ASEAN

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: In 2025, the Philippines invested 86.68 million dollars below several ASEAN competitors while

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: generating 74,758 tourist arrivals for every 1 million dollars in government marketing

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: One might say that Vietnam's smaller government branding budget is relatively lower than the Philippines,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: but it may be well to note that the Vietnam's budget is largely complemented by strong private sector investment in tourism development, particularly the Sun Group.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The gains we have achieved so far provide a strong foundation for pursuing that opportunity.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Behind these numbers are concrete interventions that strengthen our people, destinations, tourism products, and access to markets.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Let me now highlight some of the department's key accomplishments for 2025 and 2026.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: We begin with the people who deliver the tourism experience.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: As of July 2026, the department has trained 52,960.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The department has trained 168 participants nationwide, with more than half coming directly from the tourism and hospitality industry.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: We might have a slight reduction in number of trained participants this year due to recalibration and change in targeted participants,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: but it is noteworthy that by strengthening the capabilities of our workforce, academe, and LGUs,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: we build the service quality and local capacity needed for a more competitive tourism.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Apart from training, we also highlight the importance of accreditation of tourism enterprises and frontliners as it protects the quality of the tourism experience.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: DOT-accredited tourism enterprises and frontliners increased by 35% from 11,545 in 2023 to 15,592 as of June 2026.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: This year, may I note that we are going beyond accreditation numbers by strengthening compliance, monitoring, renewal, and service standards.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: All these ensure that accreditation becomes a stronger mark of quality and confidence in Philippine tourism.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Quality tourism products must also be connected to the markets that sustain them.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: As of September 2026, 20 new international routes have been created.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: These routes have been launched, opening more gateways to destinations across the country.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Another 13 routes are set to launch, bringing projected additional capacity to more than 472,000 seats by year-end.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Beyond expanding access, we are positioning the Philippines in high-value tourism markets.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: After the Philippines was recognized as the world's number one retirement destination,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: saw average SRRV applications jump from 15 to 25 per day,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: In July 2026, Bank of Singapore reported that the global longevity economy,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: driven by the growing spending power of older and retired consumers,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: is valued at $3 trillion and projected to reach,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Travel and leisure are identified among the sectors positioned to benefit from this growth.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: As the world's top-ranked retirement destination,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: the Philippines is well-positioned to capture a greater share of this growing global market.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: We are also building on our global leadership in dive tourism,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: one of the Philippines' strongest high-value tourism products.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: is estimated to generate $1.3 billion in tourism revenue, supported by our world-class marine

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: biodiversity, in seven consecutive years as the world's leading dive destination.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: But the opportunity is larger. The Philippine Commission on Sports, School with Diving,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: has identified 29 dive destination clusters and 956 dive sites nationwide.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Many of which are still emerging or undergoing development and validation.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Even under a conservative growth scenario, annual dive tourism revenue is projected to reach

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: BCSSD has certified 330 dive professionals and individuals as of June 2026.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: This builds on the strong expansion in certifications since 2023 and reflects the continued development

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: of the skilled workforce needed to support a safe, professional, and competitive Philippine dive industry.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: We are also expanding cruise tourism as a gateway to multiple Philippine destinations

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: within a single journey. Cruise calls recovered to 136 in 2025 and are projected to reach

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: 155 calls across 38 destinations by 2027, with bookings already extending into 2028.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The opportunity is to convert each port call into greater local economic activity,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: to shore excursions, longer stays, and onward travel.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Growth is already extending beyond traditional gateways, with cruise calls in the Visayas projected to double,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: from 14 in 2026 to 28 in 2027, while new destinations are being assessed for future itineraries.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Supporting this growth is the Cruise Visa Waiver Program, which makes it easier

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: for cruise passengers to enter and experience the Philippines.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Since its launch in 2024, 16,563 waivers have been issued as of June 2026,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: Notably, the 7,066 waivers issued in the first half of 2026

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: already exceeded the full year total for 2025.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: The strong uptake demonstrates the importance of streamlined travel facilitation

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: in unlocking not just the Chinese cruise market,

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay
segments.text: but all our key and emerging markets by supporting further cruise tourism growth.

segments.speaker: DOT Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay

segments.speaker: Rep. Sergio C. Dagooc
segments.text: First of all, Madam Chair, I would like to manifest my full support to the budget of the Department of Tourism.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sergio C. Dagooc
segments.text: Now, first of all, Madam Chair, I am alarmed with this issue paper of TIEZA.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sergio C. Dagooc
segments.text: May I ask, Madam Chair, DBM, bakit po outrightly dininayin ninyo yung request ng Tiesa for fund augmentation?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sergio C. Dagooc

segments.text: is in view of several legislative measures proposing the abolition of the travel tax.

segments.speaker: DBM Assistant Director Lulu P. Vispo
segments.text: However, as these bills remain under deliberation in the Senate,

segments.speaker: DBM Assistant Director Lulu P. Vispo
segments.text: yet to be enacted into law,

segments.speaker: DBM Assistant Director Lulu P. Vispo
segments.text: the Tiesa's requested subsidy was not considered in the FY2024 NEP.

segments.speaker: DBM Assistant Director Lulu P. Vispo
segments.text: And then, however, TIEZA may continue to utilize its travel tax collections to fund tourism-related infrastructure projects,

segments.text: which is consistent with Sections 72 and 73 of RA No. 9593.

segments.speaker: DBM Assistant Director Lulu P. Vispo

segments.speaker: DBM Assistant Director Lulu P. Vispo
segments.text: So, meron po rin silang mga unobligated obligation.

segments.text: Iyon na nga po, Madam Chair.

segments.text: Bakit napakabilis po ninyong mag-release ng tira doon sa mga, for lack of a better term,

segments.speaker: Rep. Sergio C. Dagooc
segments.text: So, anyway, Madam Chair, maraming salamat po.

segments.text: DBM doon sa paliwanag. Sana may parating mo kay Secretary Kim na wala naman pong legal impediment kung mag-augment tayo ng pundo.

segments.text: Madam Chair, may I ask D.O.T., mayroon po ba kayong malalim na ugnayan sa D.N.R.?

segments.text: Yung regular na ugnayan sa D.N.R.?

segments.speaker: Rep. Sergio C. Dagooc
segments.text: I'm asking that, Madam Chair, kasi I think the good Secretary will agree with me na hindi po pwedeng magkatabi yung mining at saka tourism.

segments.speaker: Rep. Sergio C. Dagooc
segments.text: That's the point I am raising.

segments.text: Madam Chair, Your Honor, we have convergence program with them, with the D.N.R.

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: So we have what we call the Sustainable Tourism Program, which aim to protect and ensure the sustainability of Philippine tourism resources and attractions.

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: So we have partners under this program, D.N.R., the WWF Philippines and the NCCA.

segments.text: Regularly, sustainable tourism, sustainable dining, and community eco-guiding.

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: So meron po kaming tulungan doon.

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: And we have conducted 13 trainings and 417 participants trained na po.

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: That's the collaboration we have under the convergence program, Your Honor, Madam Chair.

segments.text: Madam Chair, maganda pong pakinggan yung programa na yon.

segments.text: Talk with D.N.R., coordinate with D.N.R.

segments.text: Dapat itong mga area na to, wag kayong isyo ng isyo ng...

segments.text: Before we proceed, I would like to acknowledge the presence of Deputy Majority Leader Howard Guintu.

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: Madam Chair, it is being said that tourism cannot thrive.

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: Natural appeal and rich culture are only half the equation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: Sustainable growth requires supporting physical infrastructure.

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: Kailangan po ng dependable roads, airports, ports, reliable water supply, proper sanitation, telecommunications, and stable electricity.

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: While the Department of Tourism leads marketing and destination development,

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: its success hinges on interagency alignment.

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: Without synchronized investment across basic services,

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: high potential sites across our regions will remain underutilized.

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: or inaccessible to both local and international tourists.

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: In view of that, I would like to seek clarification, Secretary,

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: from the Department on the following operational points.

segments.text: kasi narinig ko kanina na sumasagot tungkol dito sa aking tanong,

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: what specific tourism sites have been identified by the Department of Tourism

segments.speaker: Rep. Salvador A. Pleyto
segments.text: as high potential but whose visitor growth remains affected by inadequate infrastructure?

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Chair, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: So, we have, as we have mentioned before,

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: domestic tourism, destination readiness, investment, and ease of entry.

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: Our key transport projects include the new Manila International Airport in Bulacan

segments.speaker: DOT Undersecretary Ma. Dionesa A. Rivera-Guillermo
segments.text: and the proposed railway connectivity between Bulacan and Clark.
